title: SMTO-CTR-0013 — A check found the task plan uses a location you didn't give

headings.title: SMTO-CTR-0013 — A check found the task plan uses a location you didn't give

html:
SMTO-CTR-0013 — A check found the task plan uses a location you didn't give

GUID: 9d89c347-1df3-4fcc-bbb2-e96d3216e3a8
Slug: task-contract-new-target
Domain: CTR · Subsystem: task-contract

What happened

  • A separate check of a Task Contract (the plan SMTO writes from a request) found it names a file, folder, web address or computer address that your request never gave. The check didn't run or change anything.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check your request for the exact file, folder, web address or computer address you meant, and write it out in full exactly as it should be used. The plan used a location that isn't in your request, so nobody can tell whether it is the right one.
  2. Send the request again as a new message so SMTO writes a new plan that uses only the locations you wrote. A newly written plan is checked from scratch against the locations in your request.
  3. Keep Task Contract Integrity Guard switched on for this conversation. The guard stops plans that invent file locations before any work starts.

What success looks like

  • The check passes for the new Task Contract, or the new task shows Task contract generated and starts working.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with your request text, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't let a task work on a location you didn't give; it may point at the wrong files or the wrong computer.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Offline validate_contract found a path, URL or IPv4 address in the contract's scope or text that is absent from the accepted source, prior contract and ingress material and is not beneath an authorized scope root.

What this means

  • Offline target inspection finds a path/address/destination absent from accepted source and outside an explicitly authorized root. This condition is produced by an explicit offline contract diagnostic, not the current compiler acceptance gate. It reports only the named check and cannot authorize execution or prove complete semantic fidelity.

Why this can happen

  • Offline target inspection finds a path/address/destination absent from accepted source and outside an explicitly authorized root.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the exact target and authorized roots, including destinations embedded in stage text.

How to fix it

  • validate_contract in src/agent_runtime/native/task_contract_models.py raised new_target: a scope root/target, or a path, URL or IPv4 address found anywhere in the contract text, does not appear verbatim in the source, prior contract or ingress and is not under a scope root that does (paths containing '..' never qualify). Correct the target to the exact one stated in the source, or state the intended location in the request; never accept a guessed destination, and keep the Integrity Guard enabled.
  • Correct the target through the supported source/contract flow; do not accept a guessed destination.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended targets are grounded in accepted source or a supported authorized root.

What not to do

  • Do not disable the integrity guard as a default fix.

Technical notes

  • This condition is produced by an explicit offline contract diagnostic, not the current compiler acceptance gate. It reports only the named check and cannot authorize execution or prove complete semantic fidelity.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
